model: Managed-care FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement stock compensation expense 204, plus ~75 of shares withheld for employee tax on vesting (FY2025 total repurchases 475 less the 400 open-market programme, 6,713k shares; CNC_Annual_FY2025.txt:4686). No combined figure is published, so the two lines are summed. 9M-2026: SBC 178, repurchases 57 (all withholding-sized). SBC is NOT excluded from Centene's adjusted EPS.
inputs.buyback_note: Open-market buybacks: FY2022 3.1bn, FY2023 1.6bn, FY2024 3.1bn, FY2025 0.4bn, 9M-2026 57 (withholding only). The programme was expanded by $2.0bn with Q3-2026 results (per CNC_Analysis.json) but nothing had been spent at 30 Sep 2026; authorised is not spent. Count held FLAT (SBC expensed); diluted shares rose from 493.1m (FY2025 weighted) to ~500m, so the flat count is a convention Centene is not yet funding. Debt: the remaining 2027 senior notes were redeemed in October 2026 (after the balance-sheet date); irrelevant to the bridge because net_debt is 0 and interest sits in the flows (FY2026 guidance 600-620).
inputs.share_count_basis: 495.068m basic shares outstanding at 23 Oct 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus 5.293m dilutive awards excluded from Q3 GAAP diluted EPS as anti-dilutive (CNC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1997) = 500.4m fully diluted. Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:03:35Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, Friday close; valuation dated Sunday)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are FCFE (after interest expense). USD build: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 1.05 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.5%. Set 50-100bp above the ELV (8.5%) and HUM (9.0%) builds in this folder because Centene is the most government-concentrated of the three (Medicaid ~57% of premium and service revenue, state-by-state rate setting and re-procurement, ACA Marketplace and stand-alone PDP set in Washington), carries more holding-company leverage relative to equity value (15.5bn debt vs ~35bn market cap), and runs the thinnest margin, so a given cost-trend miss is a larger share of earnings. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are small (total lease liabilities 761 at FY2025, CNC_Annual_FY2025.txt:4637) and rent sits inside SG&A, hence inside pretax income. One treatment: lease cost in the flows, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests immaterial (redeemable 24, nonredeemable 76 at 30 Sep 2026). Flows are attributable to Centene.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: net_debt held at ZERO by design. Holding-company debt 15,542 (LT 15,454 + current 88 at 30 Sep 2026) is charged through interest expense (678 FY2025, 466 9M-2026) inside pretax income; deducting it again would double-count. Cash 20,700, investments 17,680 (ST 2,886 + LT 14,794) and restricted deposits 1,470 are overwhelmingly held in regulated insurance subsidiaries against 21.5bn of medical claims liability and RBC requirements; they are not surplus and are not added. Investment and other income (1,572 FY2025, 1,175 9M-2026) is the return on that float and stays in the flows -- matching-asset rule satisfied because neither the income nor the asset is credited outside the flows.
inputs.ebitda_mapping: ENGINE MAPPING: ebitda_margin_path = cash pretax margin + depreciation 0.28% + P&L SBC 0.11%. 'Cash pretax' = GAAP pretax income EXCLUDING goodwill/intangible impairments and amortisation of acquired intangibles (non-cash, 685 FY2025, 488 9M-2026, running off as the 4.0bn of acquired intangibles amortise) but INCLUDING interest expense, investment income and a recurring allowance for the 'other adjustments' Centene excludes every year (restructuring/severance/contract-exit: 464 FY2023, 360 9M-2026). The engine then deducts SBC at 0.14% (P&L SBC plus equity-award withholding tax), so EBIT = cash pretax less 0.03% withholding, NOPAT = cash net income, and the engine's owner FCF = FCFE. Small conservatism: no tax shield is credited on the acquired-intangible amortisation (~150/yr for ~6 years, ~$1.5/share PV).
inputs.da_note: da_pct = depreciation only: 590 FY2025 (0.30% of revenue), 411 9M-2026 (0.27%). The 1,275 'D&A' in the cash-flow statement includes 685 of acquired-intangible amortisation, which is excluded from the pretax line instead (see ebitda_mapping) so it is not added back twice.
inputs.capex_note: Capital expenditures 767 FY2025 (0.39%), 568 9M-2026 (0.37%). capex_pct 0.38%. No acquisition allowance: Centene has been a net divester since 2022 (Magellan Rx, PANTHERx, Circle Health, Spain/UK) and the revenue path is organic.
inputs.wc_note: wc_capture_pct = -5: statutory capital retained in regulated subsidiaries at ~5% of incremental revenue (health-insurer RBC target capital is ~5-7% of premium; same convention as HUM in this folder). Medical-claims float growth is not credited: OCF is dominated by pass-through and CMS/state settlement timing (FY2024 OCF 154 vs NI 3,294; Q3-2026 OCF -3,669 'driven by the timing of pass through payments'), and over a cycle the float and the capital requirement roughly net. In the bear case the negative FY2027 growth releases capital, which is the right sign for a shrinking book.
inputs.tax_note: FY2025 income tax was a 51 benefit on a 6.7bn impairment-driven loss (largely non-deductible goodwill) -- meaningless as a base. FY2024 GAAP ETR 22.6%, FY2023 25.0%; 9M-2026 GAAP 26.0% (902 / 3,463, inflated by non-deductible items in a lower-earnings year). Cash tax 25% in FY2026, 24.5% thereafter. No NOL shelter is perpetuated.
inputs.fy2026_estimate: Year 1 = FY2026, nine months reported, anchored to the Q3-2026 guidance (earnings release 2026-10-27, recorded in CNC_Analysis.json; the 8-K itself is not among the extracted filings): adjusted EPS >$5.20 (raised $0.40), GAAP EPS >$3.46, HBR 90.4-91.1%, total revenue 196.5-200.5bn, interest expense 600-620. Revenue: 9M 154,170 already; 200bn used (+2.7%), near the top of the range because 9M grew 6.3% and the midpoint would imply a ~12% sequential Q4 drop. Cash pretax: adjusted EPS ~5.30 x ~499m = ~2.65bn adjusted NI, /0.75 = ~3.5bn adjusted pretax, less ~0.4bn of restructuring/severance that Centene excludes but which is cash = ~3.1bn = 1.55% of revenue (GAAP cross-check: 3.46 x 499 = 1.73bn NI, ~2.3bn pretax + ~0.65bn amortisation = ~2.95bn). 9M adjusted EPS was 6.45, so guidance implies a Q4 adjusted LOSS of ~$1.2/share (Q4-2025: -$1.18) -- Q4 is the seasonal HBR peak. FY2026 includes a 480 pretax benefit from final 2025 ACA risk-adjustment transfers (CNC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:2881); underlying FY2026 cash pretax is ~1.3%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Managed-care FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity via the Drivers/engine route, net_debt = 0. ROUTING: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes 'Insurer' to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B. Overridden, following the precedent already set in this folder for the two closest peers (ELV 2026-09-28, HUM 2026-09-29; also IAG.AX, GL): Centene does not compound book -- equity went 25,885 (FY2020) to 20,033 (FY2025) after 8.0bn of buybacks FY2022-24 and the 6.7bn FY2025 goodwill impairment, and 14.9bn of the remaining 22.2bn equity is goodwill and intangibles, so tangible book is ~7bn and a P/B exit would value the earnings stream on an accounting residue. Owner-FCF at WACC less net debt is also wrong: the 20.7bn cash and 17.7bn investments are regulated statutory capital (net debt undefined), and OCF is pass-through-timing noise (FY2024 154, Q3-2026 -3,669). FCFE = cash net income - (capex - depreciation) - withholding tax - statutory capital retained on growth, at the cost of equity, sidesteps both. NORMALISATION (the central judgment): this is a margin story, not a revenue story. Health benefits ratio 87.7% FY2022/23 -> 88.3% FY2024 -> 91.9% FY2025 -> 87.3/89.6/92.7% Q1/Q2/Q3-2026. Cash pretax margin on total revenue (including the zero-margin premium-tax pass-through): FY2023 3.15%, FY2024 3.01%, FY2025 0.66%, FY2026e 1.55% from guidance (incl. a 0.24pp one-off risk-adjustment true-up; underlying ~1.3%). Peak FY2023-24 margins are NOT the base mid-cycle: the revenue mix has shifted toward stand-alone PDP (IRA-inflated premium at thin margin) and premium-tax pass-through, investment yields are lower, and OBBBA work requirements from 2027 raise Medicaid acuity. Base mid-cycle cash pretax 2.4% from FY2030 (~80% of the FY2023-24 level, roughly an 89.5% HBR); bull 2.95% (back to FY2023-24); bear 1.6% (the 2026 run-rate becomes permanent). FY2027 is a second trough year in base and bear: California UIS Medi-Cal transition (~175k members), Hawaii and Florida CMS contract losses, Georgia and Texas procurement protests, OBBBA work requirements, and the 2027 Star Ratings drop (42% of MA members at 3.5+ stars vs 60%) which hits 2028 revenue. The impairment-distorted GAAP figures (EPS -13.53) are not extrapolated and neither is peak FY2024 (adjusted EPS 7.17). Terminal value is a 13x FCFE cap in base (Gordon at 9.5%/2.5% = 14.6x), Centene's long-run adjusted P/E range being ~10-15x.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case revenue path average (premium yield ~5-6%/yr less membership attrition); historical CAGRs are acquisition- and redetermination-distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.1% 3yr, -5.0% 5yr) diverges by >30% from revenue CAGR (+10.5% / +11.9%): book shrank through 8bn of buybacks FY2022-24 and the 6.7bn FY2025 goodwill impairment while revenue grew on WellCare (2020), Magellan (2022), PDP repricing under the IRA and Marketplace share gains. Neither series is a usable forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use ADJUSTED diluted EPS (FY2022 5.78 -> FY2025 2.08); GAAP EPS is negative in FY2025 so a GAAP CAGR is undefined; 5yr adjusted EPS not in the kpis table. FCF CAGRs on the owner series (reported FCF less P&L SBC; equity-award withholding not separately available for the history) are endpoint-sensitive because OCF swings by billions on pass-through and CMS settlement timing (FY2024 FCF -490). Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are essentially identical: SBC is ~0.1% of revenue and immaterial to growth.

base.ebitda_margin_note: = cash pretax [1.55, 1.75, 2.05, 2.25, 2.40 flat] + depreciation 0.28 + P&L SBC 0.11. FY2026 from the Q3-2026 guidance (adjusted EPS >$5.20, GAAP >$3.46, HBR 90.4-91.1%), which includes a 0.24pp one-off risk-adjustment true-up (underlying ~1.3%); FY2027 1.75% on Marketplace repricing, workforce-buyout SG&A savings and lower interest, net of contract losses and OBBBA acuity; FY2028-30 Medicaid rates catch up with acuity; mid-cycle 2.4% is ~80% of FY2023-24.
base.narrative: Trough-and-partial-recovery. FY2026 revenue +2.7% to ~200bn (top of the 196.5-200.5bn guidance; 9M ran +6%) on premium yield against an 8% membership decline; FY2027 flat as California UIS, Hawaii, Florida CMS and OBBBA work-requirement disenrollment offset rate increases; then 4-5% on Medicaid rate/acuity catch-up, PDP and D-SNP integration, decaying to 3%. Cash pretax margin 1.55% in FY2026 (guidance-implied, including a one-off 480 risk-adjustment true-up), 1.75% in FY2027, recovering to 2.4% by FY2030 (HBR ~89.5%) and holding -- below FY2023-24 because of the PDP/premium-tax mix shift and lower investment yields. Cost of equity 9.5%, 13x FCFE cap.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: = cash pretax [1.60, 2.10, 2.50, 2.80, 2.95 flat] + 0.39. Back to the FY2023-24 cash pretax margin (3.0-3.15%) less a recurring-charge allowance by FY2030.
bull.narrative: Medicaid rate adequacy resets to acuity in the 2027 cycle (as it did after the 2017-18 ACA expansion cohort), Georgia and Texas protests succeed or are replaced by the Arizona ALTCS rebid (October 2027 start), the Marketplace pool stabilises after the enhanced-APTC expiry and Centene's 2026 repricing of 95% of the book holds, and the D-SNP integration mandate (2027 restrictions, 2030 full) channels dual eligibles into Centene's overlapping Medicaid/MA footprint. Enterprise-optimisation savings (adjusted SG&A ratio already 6.5% in Q3-2026 vs 7.0%) stick. Cash pretax back to ~2.95% by FY2030 and revenue 6-6.5% in FY2028-30. 14x cap.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: = cash pretax [1.50, 1.30, 1.40, 1.50, 1.60 flat] + 0.39. HBR stays ~91-92%; the FY2026 underlying margin (ex the one-off risk-adjustment true-up) becomes the new normal.
bear.narrative: States keep setting Medicaid rates on lagged, healthier-cohort experience while OBBBA work requirements (2027) and six-monthly redeterminations strip healthier expansion members and raise acuity; Georgia and Texas re-procurements are lost on top of California UIS, Hawaii and Florida CMS, so FY2027 revenue falls 4%; the Marketplace morbidity shift after APTC expiry persists; the Star Ratings drop to 42% at 3.5+ costs MA bonus revenue from 2028; and PDP risk corridors (narrowed in 2025, removed in 2026) expose Centene to IRA Part D cost trend. Cash pretax settles at 1.6%, roughly the FY2026 underlying margin ex one-offs. Terminal growth 2%, 11x cap.

scenario_narratives.base: Trough-and-partial-recovery: FY2026-27 are the trough years (HBR ~91-92%, contract losses and OBBBA acuity in 2027), then state Medicaid rates catch up with acuity and Marketplace repricing holds, taking the cash pretax margin to 2.4% by FY2030 -- about 80% of the FY2023-24 level, because PDP and premium-tax pass-through now dilute the margin on total revenue and investment yields are lower. Revenue grows on premium yield, not membership.
scenario_narratives.bull: Full margin recovery: Medicaid rate adequacy resets to acuity in the 2027 cycle, procurement protests go Centene's way, the ACA pool stabilises after the subsidy expiry, D-SNP integration channels duals into Centene's overlapping Medicaid/MA footprint, and enterprise-optimisation SG&A savings stick. Cash pretax back to ~2.95% (FY2023-24) by FY2030 with 6-6.5% revenue growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural impairment of the Medicaid franchise's margin: lagged state rate-setting, OBBBA-driven acuity, Georgia/Texas contract losses on top of California, Hawaii and Florida, a persistently sicker Marketplace pool and Part D cost exposure after the risk corridors were removed. Revenue falls 4% in FY2027 and the cash pretax margin settles at 1.6% (HBR stuck above 91%).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: earnings depend on government payers set by 30 state Medicaid agencies, CMS and Congress (OBBBA, APTC expiry, IRA Part D), management's cost-trend visibility failed badly in 2025 (guidance withdrawn July 2025, 6.7bn impairment), and Q3-2026 HBR of 92.7% shows the recovery is not yet visible in the run-rate. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs Medicaid rate adequacy, favourable procurement outcomes and a stable ACA pool all at once, each outside management's control. Base 50%: a partial recovery is the modal outcome for a Medicaid MCO -- rate-setting lags acuity but does catch up (2017-19 precedent) -- and FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to >$5.20 (from $2.08 in FY2025) with HBR narrowed to 90.4-91.1%, so the 2025 trough was partly one-off.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Centene is valued on normalised FCFE (cash net income less statutory capital retention) capitalised at a 9.5% cost of equity, with holding-company debt charged through interest in the flows and regulated cash and investments left with the reserves they back. The valuation turns almost entirely on one number -- the mid-cycle pretax margin on ~$200bn of mostly government-funded premium. Every 0.1pp of mid-cycle pretax margin is ~$0.2bn of pretax income, roughly $3-4 per share of value. Neither the impairment-distorted FY2025 GAAP result nor peak FY2024 margins are extrapolated; the base assumes ~80% recovery toward FY2023-24 profitability.
key_risks_to_valuation: Medicaid rate adequacy: states set rates on lagged experience while redeterminations and OBBBA work requirements (from 2027) raise the acuity of the remaining population.
Procurement: Georgia and Texas award protests, Arizona ALTCS rebid (award early 2027); losses compound California UIS, Hawaii and Florida CMS exits.
ACA Marketplace: morbidity shift after enhanced-APTC expiry; Marketplace membership already down from 5.5m (FY2025) to 3.4m (Q3-2026).
Medicare: 2027 Star Ratings fell to 42% of MA members at 3.5+ stars (60% prior year), hitting 2028 revenue; PDP risk corridors removed for 2026 under the IRA Part D redesign.
Holding-company leverage: 15.5bn debt against a ~35bn market cap leaves less buffer than ELV/UNH if a second margin shock arrives; buybacks are suspended.
Cash flow visibility: OCF swings by billions on pass-through and settlement timing (Q3-2026 -3.7bn), so FCFE is modelled from earnings, not from reported FCF.
